newsitem.title: UK: NATS cuts ATC charges at BAA London and Scottish airports.
newsitem.headline: NATS cuts ATC charges at BAA London and Scottish airports.

text.p: The Britain's National Air Traffic Services (NATS) is reducing air traffic charges (ATC) to airlines operating from BAA's London and Scottish Airports, the state air traffic body said.
This is in line with its strategic objective of keeping increases within the rate of inflation and, where possible, reducing them.

"These substantial reductions have been achieved by a continuing programme of improving cost control and efficiency throughout National Air Traffic Services while, of course, maintaining our high safety standards,", NATS Chief Executive Derek MeLauchian said on Wednesday.
"Only seven per cent of flights handled last summer were subject to air traffic control delay, despite a five per cent increase in air fraffic."
At Heathrow, Gatwick and Stansted the fees are being cut by 7 percent. This is the fifth year running that charges have been reduced at the London Airports.
In Scotland charges are being reduced at Aberdeen by 13 per cent, Edinburgh by 15 per cent and Glasgow by 16 per cent.
NATS - part of the Civil Aviation Authority - is also reducing the charge per flight for North Atlantic air traffic control services by 18 per cent.
NATS provides ATC services for airlines at Manchester, Birmingham, Cardiff, Belfast and London City airports under separate individual contracts.
ATC charges in sterling a tonne at BAA's airports and North Atlantic for years starting April 1 include:

Heathrow/Gatwick/Stansted
Each Additional tonne 0.52 0.56 0.65 0.69 0.73
